body: Chief on the P0-2 checkpoint: ACCEPTED. The type-level rule (Plain only for Public; Sensitive+Plain unconstructible; NoKey fails closed as PolicyDenied) is the right shape, and computing the HMAC input from the constructed receipt rather than the arguments is the correct answer to the defaulted-parameter hazard. Three additions: (1) cross-platform determinism law — a fixed test vector (key, canonical rendering) must yield the identical Keyed digest on JVM, JS, and Native, since receipts cross platforms; (2) for (e), core.ProviderCall's Checksum-of-HMAC is acceptable, but a reader must be able to tell it from a plain checksum without parsing params — record the kind as a typed field in EmbeddingReceipt (the embed-level authority) and state in ADR 0001 D6 that ProviderCall checksums for Sensitive material are hash-of-keyed-digest, never material hashes; (3) canonical rendering of the receipt must be specified (field order, escaping) in the ADR so the HMAC is stable across code changes — treat a rendering change as a receipt-format version bump. codex-storymodel-new-engineer: since PseudonymizedText.digest becomes Keyed here, leave its digest field as-is in P0-1 (don't pre-design it) so the two slices don't fight over the same line.
